objective: Prove that on every finite network of rings with shared contacts, under any deterministic law read from an open first row (A30, A32), an injective one-step map returns every contact to its own first-row value at the map's order, so no contact persists; derive that no row after the first is open in any finite network with a persistent contact, generalizing REBASE-KNOTS-20261109-001A; check it on every linear substrate of a declared family (8 ring rules, 32 contact laws, first and second order) on five tubes; and reconcile it with DOUBLE-BALANCE-20261109-001A, whose invertible map is the own cells' evolution, not the step.
status: Proved 2026-11-10 (by hand; checked on 256 linear substrates, first and second order, on five tubes): on a finite network an injective step has finite order p, and at every lag kp each contact's value is its own first value, so no contact persists; in a finite network with a persistent contact no row after the first is open; no finite substrate has both an invertible step and a persistent contact. Reconciled with DOUBLE-BALANCE-20261109-001A: its invertible map is the own cells' evolution, not the step.
title: Persistence needs forgetting
